To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in vivo activation of murine NK cells by a tiloring analogue prolongs survival and prevents metastasis formation in syngeneic tumour systems.
in vivo activation of NK cells with tilorone prolongs survival and reduces metastasis formation.

a single dose of tilorone analogue administered to mice before injection of different tumour cell lines significantly increases the survival time of the mice and inhibits metastatic colonization of the lungs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of NK cells and their activation in the control of metastatic growth in vivo.
the effect of in vivo NK cell activation by the tilorones on the survival of animals with metastatic disease.
the study of a novel class of synthetic tilorone derivatives, with a particular emphasis on their immunomodulating properties, and with the study of their effects on the natural killer cell system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tilorone‐NK cell system is an important mechanism in tumour resistance and metastasis prevention.
the NK cell system is involved in the inhibition of metastases formation by the tilorones, and that this effect is not dependent on a single tumour line.
the NK cell system is a key component of the host's defence against the development of tumours.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NK cells are the most important effector cells in the host defence against metastasis formation.
the NK cell‐activating agent we tested, RMI 10, 874DA, has the potential to be used as an adjunctive therapy in cancer treatment.
NK activation in vivo by a tilorome analogue prolongs the survival of mice and inhibits metastatic growth of tumours.
The main takeaway from our work is that

NK cell activation can have a significant effect on the outcome of metastatic spread, and that it may be possible to modulate the immune system in vivo in such a way as to increase the effectiveness of immunotherapy.
NK cells are involved in controlling metastasis formation and that their activation in vivo by tilorone‐like compounds is an effective approach for the control of metastatic disease.
the tilorone analog RMI 10, 874 DA, is a promising agent for the treatment of NK‐sensitive tumours.
